text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Department store chain Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer (KBB) gives profits warning. (p1)
- Restructuring of Dutch credit insurer NCM will cost 225 of the company's 1,300 jobs. (p1)
- Teak funds seek to place their investment products under Dutch central bank's supervision. (p1)
- KPN, the Dutch post and telecoms group, says it is not concerned by reports that major shareholder in TNT, Bankers Trust of Australia, describes KPN's bid as "on the low side". (p1)
- Dutch oil company NAM finds gas under the Wadden Sea in the north of the Netherlands. (p3)
- Technical trading company Geveke aims to double its profit to Dfl 40 million before 2000. (p3)
- ING Group sidelined by other banks in developing multi-functional chipcard. (p3)
- Economic affairs minister launches three venture capital companies aimed at high-tech firms. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- PM Kok presses environmental and transport ministers to reach agreement on Beek airfield, near Maastricht, and the night flights there. (p1)
- Rabobank orders one million chipcard scanners from Datelnet of Den Bosch. (p2)
- Samsung guarantees to build Fokker planes in the Netherlands after 2001. (p2)
- Unions go to court over ABN Amro bank's refusal to apply pay and conditions for banking sector to its call-centres. (p33)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch state claims 75 tonnes of gold, worth some Dfl 1.5 bn that was stolen by Nazis and put in Swiss bank vaults. (p1)
- Korea's Samsung and Dutch state not yet near a takeover agreement. (p35)
- Retailer Vendex utterly surprised by KBB's profit warning a day after Vendex announced to shed its 36 pct stake. (p35)
- Rising demand for property. (p37)
TROUW
- Philips Electronics better known in India than Coca-Cola. (p6)
- Poor knowledge of French is costing Dutch businesses Dfl 20 bn a year. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Shipping and tank storage company Van Ommeren seeks to takeover Sweden's tank-owner Brostroms. (p11)
- Rabobank invests $24 million (Dfl 41 million) in new brewery near Bucharest, Romania. (p13)
